adjudication_records.issue_text: P1 slots.ts ~line 103: dayjs objects compared with === (object identity), always false, making zero-length-override check dead code
P0 slots.ts ~line 128: return true on override day bypasses busy.every() booking-conflict check, allowing double-booking on override days

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts` `checkIfIsAvailable()`, after the new date-override logic, the code does `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` before reaching the final `return busy.every(...)` conflict check. That means on any day where a matching date override is detected (even if the slot is within the override window), the function can return `true` without checking `busy`, potentially marking a slot as available even when it overlaps an existing booking/busy time. The only earlier conflict guard is a narrow `currentSeats` exact-start-time check, not a general overlap check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1 slots.ts ~line 136-148: working-hours check compares invitee-local slot time against organizer-local working hours, producing false available/unavailable slots for differing timezones

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts` within `checkIfIsAvailable`, the “normal work hours” gate uses `slotStartTime = time.utc()` and then compares `slotStartTime.day()` / `slotStartTime.hour()` (UTC-based) against `workingHours` (`workingHour.days`, `startTime`, `endTime`) without converting the slot into the organizer’s timezone (even though `organizerTimeZone` is available and used for dateOverrides). If `workingHours` are defined in organizer-local minutes-of-day/days (as is typical), this will misclassify availability when organizer and invitee timezones differ. The diff shows no timezone normalization for working-hours, so the finding is grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2 lib/slots.ts ~line 212: override.timeZone may be undefined causing dayjs(...).tz(undefined) to throw and crash slot generation; also fragile date stringification round-trip

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts`, the new logic unconditionally calls `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()`. The diff also makes `timeZone` on `TimeRange` optional (`packages/types/schedule.d.ts`), and `getSchedule` populates `timeZone: availability.timeZone` which itself may be undefined. That means `override.timeZone` can be undefined at runtime, making the `.tz(override.timeZone)` call potentially crash or behave incorrectly during slot generation. Additionally, using `override.start.toString()` introduces a fragile string round-trip vs using the `Date` directly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2 slots.ts ~line 490: organizerTimeZone set to schedule.timeZone bypassing the fallback chain, shifting override windows incorrectly when schedule lacks a timezone

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts`, the new `checkIfIsAvailable` logic uses `organizerTimeZone` to compute a UTC offset for date overrides (`organizerTimeZone ? dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1 : 0`). But the call site at `+489` now passes `organizerTimeZone: schedule.timeZone`. If `schedule.timeZone` is undefined, this bypasses the earlier fallback chain (now stored in `organizerTimeZone` variable) and forces the offset to 0, which can mis-evaluate override windows for organizers with a non-UTC timezone. The diff itself shows both the dependency on `organizerTimeZone` and the potentially-undefined value being passed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3 slots.ts ~line 118: boundary condition isAfter excludes slot starting exactly at override end, returning it as available with no remaining override time

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` the date override exclusion logic treats slots as outside the override only when `slotStartTime.isAfter(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset,"minutes"))`. If a slot starts exactly at the override end (`slotStartTime.isSame(end)`), this condition is false, so the `find(...)` callback does not return `true` (i.e., does not mark it “outside”), while `dateOverrideExist` is set to true for that day and the function then returns `true` (available). This makes a slot starting exactly at the override end incorrectly available with no remaining override time; it likely should use `isSame`/`isSameOrAfter` for the end boundary.

adjudication_records.issue_text: O(N×M) linear scans inside per-slot availability check: checkIfIsAvailable adds two Array.find scans (dateOverrides.find and workingHours.find) per call, making it O(N·M·(D+W)); precompute per-day override/working-hour maps once before the slot loop

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `checkIfIsAvailable` now performs `dateOverrides.find(...)` and `workingHours.find(...)` on every invocation (see added blocks around the new date override and working-hours checks). `checkIfIsAvailable` is called inside per-slot loops in `getSchedule` (multiple `.filter`/loops over computed slots), so this introduces additional linear scans per slot, creating an avoidable performance regression when slots/overrides/working-hours grow. This is a diff-grounded efficiency concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Redundant repeated dayjs construction per override in getSlots: each override constructs dayjs(override.start.toString()) twice plus duplicate dayjs(...).utc().add(offset) computations for startTime and endTime; hoist into single variables

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts`, the new `activeOverrides.flatMap` callback repeatedly constructs `dayjs(...)` objects: `dayjs(override.start.toString())` is called twice to compute offsets, and `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute")` is recomputed separately for `.hour()` and `.minute()` (same for `override.end`). This is redundant work per override and could be hoisted into variables without changing behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Object identity comparison of dayjs objects with === in slots.ts:~110 is always false; zero-length-override check never fires; should use .isSame()/.valueOf()

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a strict identity comparison between two newly-created Dayjs objects: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")) { ... }` inside `checkIfIsAvailable` (in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts`). Since these are distinct objects, `===` will never be true, so the intended “zero-length override” case will never trigger; it should use `.isSame(...)`/`.valueOf()` etc. (The finding cites `slots.ts`, but the defect is clearly present in the shown diff.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Working-hours end check uses slot start time instead of slot end time (end is a copy of start) at slots.ts:~135, letting late-running slots slip through working-hour boundaries
P1: Early return true when dateOverrideExist at slots.ts:~120-125 skips the busy/booking check, causing double-booking risk on override days

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` (viewer/slots.ts), after evaluating `dateOverrides`, the code does `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` before the final `return busy.every(...)` block. This means that when any date override exists for the slot’s day (even if the slot is within the override window), the function returns `true` without checking `busy` (calendar conflicts) or other booking constraints, which can allow offering a slot that overlaps an existing busy period (double-booking risk).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Sign-error risk in organizer-timezone offset conversion — negating utcOffset() and adding it shifts UTC time in wrong direction at slots.ts:~103, inconsistent with packages/lib/slots.ts companion implementation

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts), the code computes `utcOffset = dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` and then applies it via `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` for date-override comparisons. This shifts the override timestamps by the negated organizer offset without considering the invitee timezone, and it is inconsistent with the companion offset-handling in `packages/lib/slots.ts`, which computes a relative offset (`inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset`) before shifting. Given that `date.start`/`date.end` are already absolute `Date` instants, applying an extra negated organizer offset is very likely to move the instants in the wrong direction and misclassify slots as inside/outside overrides.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: slotStartTime.day() evaluated in UTC while workingHours.days are in organizer timezone, causing wrong weekday matching near midnight UTC at slots.ts:~132

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, `slotStartTime` is explicitly converted to UTC (`const slotStartTime = time.utc();`), and the working-hours gate uses `slotStartTime.day()` to match `workingHour.days`. However, `workingHours` are passed in without any timezone normalization, and the function even receives `organizerTimeZone` but does not use it when evaluating weekdays/hours. This makes weekday matching dependent on UTC rather than the organizer’s schedule timezone, which will misclassify slots around midnight UTC for non-UTC organizer timezones.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Inconsistent timezone source for overrides — dateOverrides flattened with availability.timeZone but checkIfIsAvailable uses eventType/schedule/userAvailability timezone, causing boundary-day mismatches

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `timeZone: availability.timeZone` onto each flattened `dateOverride` (getSchedule: `availability.dateOverrides.map(... timeZone: availability.timeZone ...)`), but `checkIfIsAvailable` ignores per-override timezone entirely and instead applies a single `organizerTimeZone` to all `dateOverrides` when computing `utcOffset` (`dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset()`). Since `dateOverrides` can include overrides from different users (and now explicitly carry their own `timeZone`), using `organizerTimeZone` rather than `date.timeZone` can misinterpret override boundaries (especially around day boundaries) and incorrectly accept/reject slots.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: New test doesn't actually cover the changed behavior — it only asserts slots are unchanged when the invitee timezone matches an already-covered scenario, and the offset-translation logic in packages/lib/slots.ts:208-227 is untested (apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts:787-803)

adjudication.rationale: The newly added test explicitly changes the invitee `timeZone` to `Timezones["+6:00"]` while using the same UTC `startTime`/`endTime`, and then asserts the returned slots. That directly exercises the new offset-translation logic in `packages/lib/slots.ts` (which depends on the invitee `timeZone` vs `override.timeZone`). The claim that it "matches an already-covered scenario" or that the translation logic is "untested" is not verifiable from the shown diff; the added test does cover the changed path at least indirectly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Object identity comparison instead of value comparison — comparing two distinct Dayjs objects with === is always false, making the zero-length override early-exit dead code with no test coverage (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:~109)

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` the code checks `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")) { return true; }`. This uses strict object identity on two newly-created Dayjs instances, which will not be `===` even when they represent the same instant. That makes the intended “zero-length override” branch effectively unreachable, so behavior for `start == end` overrides is incorrect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Working-hours end check uses the slot start instead of the slot end — slotEndTime is never used, so slots starting inside working hours but ending after workingHour.endTime are wrongly treated as within working hours (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:~146-147)

adjudication.rationale: In the new working-hours check inside `checkIfIsAvailable` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts), `end` is computed from `slotStartTime` again (`const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`) instead of using `slotEndTime`. As a result, the condition `end > workingHour.endTime` can never detect slots that start within working hours but extend past `workingHour.endTime`, matching the finding that `slotEndTime` is effectively not used for this check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: dateOverrideExist short-circuit skips the busy/bookings check entirely, returning available without consulting busy on date-override days, creating a double-booking risk (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:~126-129)

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, once a date override exists for the slot’s day and the slot is *within* the override window (i.e., the `dateOverrides.find(...)` does not trigger the “outside override” early-return), the code hits `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` and returns availability immediately. This happens before the `busy.every(...)` block that checks conflicts with existing busy times/bookings, so on override days a slot can be marked available even if it overlaps `busy`, creating a double-booking risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: The new override/working-hours gating in checkIfIsAvailable has no unit tests at all — edge cases like slots ending exactly at override start, spanning override boundaries, and undefined organizerTimeZone (offset defaulting to 0) are untested (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:99-152)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new gating logic in `checkIfIsAvailable` for date overrides and working hours (e.g., early `return false/true` based on comparisons around `slotStartTime/slotEndTime`, and an offset calculation when `organizerTimeZone` is undefined defaulting to `0`). The only test added in this diff (`getSchedule.test.ts`) is an integration-style `getSchedule` case about a date override in a different timezone returning the same UTC slots; it does not exercise the specific boundary/edge conditions mentioned (slot ending exactly at override start, spanning override boundaries, undefined `organizerTimeZone`). So the concern is diff-grounded and actionable as missing coverage for newly introduced nontrivial logic, not a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Sign/semantics of offset in slots.ts are untested and fragile — re-parsing a Date.toString() makes offsets depend on the server's local timezone, and DST-correctness of deriving override.end's shift from override.start's offset is untested (packages/lib/slots.ts:211-213)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts` the new offset computation uses `dayjs(override.start.toString())` before `.tz(...)` (lines around 211-213). `Date#toString()` is locale/server-timezone dependent, so parsing it can change behavior depending on the server’s TZ, making the computed `utcOffset()` potentially wrong. Additionally, the single `offset` is derived from `override.start` but then applied to both `override.start` and `override.end`, which can be incorrect if the override spans a DST boundary (end offset differs from start). The added test exercises a different timezone scenario but does not cover server-local-TZ parsing or DST-span correctness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Spreading ...override after timeZone in slots.ts:~411 means a stored override with its own timeZone field would silently overwrite availability.timeZone, with no test distinguishing which timezone source wins

adjudication.rationale: In `getSchedule` the dateOverrides are built as `{ userId, timeZone: availability.timeZone, ...override }`, so if an individual `override` object contains a `timeZone` field (now possible since `TimeRange` was extended with `timeZone?: string` in `packages/types/schedule.d.ts`), it will silently override `availability.timeZone`. The diff doesn’t establish or test the intended precedence between `availability.timeZone` vs `override.timeZone` (the added test only varies the *input* timezone, not an override’s own timezone), so the review concern about ambiguous “which wins” is valid, though not provably a functional defect without more context on stored override data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: checkIfIsAvailable: on any day with a date override, the busy/booking check is bypassed because `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` executes before the `busy.every(...)` check, causing double-booking risk

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the newly added date-override logic can return before the busy/booking overlap logic runs. Specifically, after the `dateOverrides.find(...)` block, the function does `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` (added around lines ~99-150), which makes any slot that falls within a matching date override immediately “available” without reaching the subsequent `return busy.every((busyTime) => { ... })` check. This can allow offering slots that overlap existing busy times/bookings on days where a date override exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Copy-paste bug: working-hours end check uses slotStartTime for both start and end, so `end === start` always and slots starting within working hours but ending after them are incorrectly offered
Dayjs objects compared with `===` are always unequal; the intended zero-length-override check never triggers and should use `isSame`
matched_golden_ids: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same underlying bug: comparing Dayjs objects with `===` checks reference equality so it won’t work for value comparison, and recommends using `isSame()` instead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: organizerTimeZone passed to checkIfIsAvailable is actually the per-availability (host) timezone, can be undefined (falling back to utcOffset=0), and overrides are not interpreted with their own override.timeZone, shifting override times incorrectly

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, date override evaluation uses only the `organizerTimeZone` parameter to compute an offset (`dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1`), and the `dateOverrides` type passed in is `{start,end}[]` (no timezone). Yet in `getSchedule` the overrides are now enriched with `timeZone: availability.timeZone` and `TimeRange` gained `timeZone?: string`, but that per-override timezone is never consumed in `checkIfIsAvailable`. Additionally, call sites pass `organizerTimeZone: schedule.timeZone` / `userSchedule?.timeZone`, which can be `undefined`, triggering the `: 0` fallback offset. This matches the finding: overrides are not interpreted using their own timezone and can be shifted/compared incorrectly when `organizerTimeZone` is missing or differs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In packages/lib/slots.ts, `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` silently falls back to server-local timezone when override.timeZone is undefined, and toString() round-tripping plus computing offset only at override.start ignores DST differences

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` in `packages/lib/slots.ts` without guarding `override.timeZone`. In this PR, `timeZone` is newly added to the override objects and is typed as optional (`packages/types/schedule.d.ts`), so it is plausible for `override.timeZone` to be `undefined`, making the offset calculation dependent on Dayjs's handling of an undefined TZ (fallback/throw). Also, the code computes a single `offset` based only on `override.start` and applies it to both `override.start` and `override.end`, which could be incorrect across DST boundaries, though whether such ranges occur isn’t provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Slots on an override day that end before the override starts are hard-blocked (find callback returns true → slot rejected), making the rest of the day unavailable even during normal working hours

adjudication.rationale: The new logic in `checkIfIsAvailable` explicitly treats a date override as defining the only allowed availability for that day: if an override exists for the slot’s day (`dateOverrideExist = true`) then any slot outside the override window (including those whose `slotEndTime` is before/at `date.start`) is intentionally rejected via the `dateOverrides.find(...)` → `return false` path (“// slot is not within the date override”). This does not “make the rest of the day unavailable” beyond blocking times outside the override, which appears to be the intended semantics per the in-code comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new test in getSchedule.test.ts asserting override-timezone case equals plain-UTC result cannot distinguish correct UTC handling from offset logic never executing; it doesn't cover an override timezone differing from the slot query timezone

adjudication.rationale: The added test calls `getSchedule` with `timeZone: Timezones["+6:00"]` and then asserts the returned slots are the same UTC timestamps as the prior case (comment: “it should return the same as this is the utc time”). From the diff, the new override-timezone adjustment logic is in `packages/lib/slots.ts` (computing `offset = inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset` using `override.timeZone` vs the requested `timeZone`). The new test does not explicitly set/verify an override `timeZone` that differs from the query timezone nor assert any behavior that would fail if `offset` were effectively 0 (e.g., because override/timeZone match or because the adjustment isn’t applied). This is a specific coverage gap for the newly introduced offset logic, not a demonstrated runtime defect.
